test.why: S3: PYTHONPATH entries come before site-packages on sys.path, so ./src wins over an installed copy. Unverified design choices: -q, and that dependencies and test tools must already be installed (the run installs nothing; the package itself need not be, because of PYTHONPATH=src).

conventions.rule: Name test files test_*.py or *_test.py so pytest discovers them.
Keep tests in a directory outside the application code.
Develop against an editable install of the package, as pytest suggests; the seed test command still puts ./src first.

In a src layout the package must be installed to be tested, which guards against importing the in-development copy by accident; strict runs deliberately import the clone's ./src (PYTHONPATH=src), so here the layout is what matters, not an install.
Call pytest as python -m pytest when the current directory must be importable; the bare pytest command does not add it.
Keep pytest settings in pyproject.toml under [tool.pytest.ini_options] (or another supported config file).
If the project sets a minimum coverage, enforce it with pytest-cov's --cov-fail-under.
Format code with ruff format; --check lists files that would change and exits non-zero without writing.
Module names are short and all lowercase.

dod.item: pytest exits 0: every collected test passes
ruff format --check reports no unformatted files
Coverage stays at or above the project's minimum, when one is set

S1.evidence: pytest's good-practices page: discovery looks for test_*.py and *_test.py files, tests may live in a separate directory outside the application code, and developing against an editable install is recommended.

S2.evidence: Running pytest through the interpreter is nearly the same as the pytest script, except that the interpreter variant also adds the current directory to sys.path.

S3.evidence: Python builds sys.path in a fixed order: PYTHONPATH entries are added before the standard library, and site-packages directories come last; with -m the current directory is the first entry.

S4.evidence: The src layout helps avoid accidental use of the in-development copy of the code, and it requires the package to be installed (for example in development mode) before it can be tested.

S5.evidence: A pyproject.toml with a [tool.pytest.ini_options] table is one of the places pytest reads its configuration from.

S6.evidence: pytest exit code 0 means all collected tests passed; exit code 1 means tests ran but some failed.

S7.evidence: ruff check is the linter's main entry point; without a path it lints the current directory, and by default it exits 1 when violations are found and 0 when there are none.

S8.evidence: ruff format without a path formats the current directory; with --check it writes nothing and exits non-zero when any file would be reformatted.

S9.evidence: pytest-cov's --cov option takes an optional path or package to measure, and --cov-fail-under fails the run when total coverage is below the given minimum.

S10.evidence: pip-audit scans Python environments for packages with known vulnerabilities; pip-audit . audits a local project, and it exits 0 when none are found and 1 when some are.

S11.evidence: PEP 8 says modules should have short, all-lowercase names.

S12.evidence: The ruff fix setting turns automatic fixing on by default and is overridden by the --fix and --no-fix command-line flags, so --no-fix lets a check run without rewriting files even when a project sets fix = true.
